next_steps: Two findings are recorded in .audit/ with evidence but deliberately NOT fixed, and both should stay unfixed until there is evidence they matter: (1) ~29 of the cancelled guards the sweep added sit after the last state write and protect nothing, worth ~60 cosmetic lines across 29 files -- a regex codemod was attempted and silently deleted an await, so it was reverted; doing it by hand on merged+deployed code is a bad risk trade. (2) lib/booking/store.ts:217 calls dispatch during render, which reaches saveDraft -> sessionStorage.setItem, so in theory a discarded render could persist a draft -- but no test could be built to discriminate it (two attempts both passed on the old code because preselected === service disarms the write after the first commit), and moving the write into an effect measurably regressed app/admin/bookings/__tests__/calendar.test.tsx (passes 4.5s on main, times out at 20s+ with the fix, 3 consecutive runs) because main commits draft.date synchronously during render. Revisit only if a real discarded render appears on the booking page (Suspense or an error boundary).

app/admin/bookings/__tests__/walkin.test.tsx and calendar.test.tsx have almost no timing headroom: they run 2-22s against a 20s testTimeout and fail spuriously whenever tsc or a full-project eslint runs concurrently. Re-run them in isolation before treating a failure as a regression. Consider raising testTimeout for that directory or cutting the work they do.

If touching lib/booking/store.ts again, the ordering constraint is load-bearing: dispatch during render makes draft.date available to the same commit, and the calendar depends on that. Any change that defers the write by one render breaks that test.
